claim: The owner atom's exact token for the fourth finding class, "unsupported or already-covered", is not preserved anywhere in the compile, and the class is spelled three different ways inside ERS-004 alone.
evidence: atom-external-research-owner-canon exact_tokens includes "unsupported or already-covered"; ERS-004 declares preserved_exact_tokens: [... "unsupported or already-covered" ...] but its text uses "unsupported_or_covered" four times (canonical_text "or unsupported_or_covered, a proposal the product already owns"; acceptance "exactly one of correction, capability, product_choice or unsupported_or_covered"; "The unsupported_or_covered count is never reported as a false-positive rate") and "unsupported-or-covered" once (negative constraint "Do not report unsupported-or-covered counts as a false-positive rate"). The declared token occurs in no unit body.
suggested_repair: Fix one identifier for the class in ERS-004 and use the ledger's exact token when naming it in prose.

claim: The product-choice class identifier drifts across the five units that name it, so the contract family's 30 negative fixtures have no single enum value to key on.
evidence: ERS-001 and PLS-023 write "product choice"; ERS-004 writes both "product choice" (canonical_text) and "product_choice" (acceptance); ERS-005 writes "product_choice" twice; ERS-007 writes all three forms; ACD-467 writes "product-choice". ATS-054 encodes "that a correction cannot be routed to a user decision" in the fixtures without ever naming the enum spelling.
suggested_repair: Declare the four class values once in ERS-004 as the enum the schema uses and reference that spelling everywhere else.

claim: The unit that defines the stage names does not use the stage identifiers it declares preserved, and the rest of the compile uses the other spelling.
evidence: ERS-002 declares preserved_exact_tokens: ["discovery", "implementation", "history", "reconcile", "compare", ...] but its canonical_text says "reconciliation against the frozen plans snapshot, and comparison producing findings"; neither "reconcile" nor "compare" appears in ERS-002. ERS-012 uses the campaign spellings ("reconcile 3,699.3 s and compare 658.3 s"), as does the evidence shard.
suggested_repair: Name the five stages in ERS-002 as discovery, implementation, history, reconcile and compare, and use the descriptive words only as gloss.

claim: ERS-002's stage chain has no review stage, yet ERS-010 configures "a topic's review stage" and ERS-011 adds an optional breadth stage alongside it, so the atom's "review configuration and the optional breadth stage" obligation is compiled with no place in the pipeline; "independent review" is also used for two different things.
evidence: ERS-002: "five research stages in order - discovery ..., and comparison producing findings - followed by blind adjudication against a union, an independent review, and landing through a ledger", and its acceptance "Adjudication, independent review and ledger landing follow the research stages". ERS-010: "A topic's review stage runs one strong model with a turn budget". ERS-011: "A topic may add an optional breadth stage on a cheap model alongside the strong review". ERS-006's "independent review" is instead "an agent that ran no research job and scored no arm".
suggested_repair: Place the review stage and the optional breadth stage in ERS-002's stage order and rename one of the two uses of "independent review" so the correction reviewer and the review arms are distinct terms.

claim: ERS-003's closed input list and its negative constraint forbid exactly what ERS-010, ERS-011 and ERS-012 describe the review and breadth arms doing, so a review arm could not pass the admission check the same unit says fails closed.
evidence: ERS-003: "A research job admits exactly three input classes: the frozen plans snapshot ..., the product brief, and the job's own arm artifacts from earlier stages of the same topic", negative constraint "Do not let a research stage read another arm's artifacts", and "a job whose declared inputs do not hash to the recorded values fails closed before dispatch". ERS-012: "Review-only arms over frozen research artifacts ran between 668.7 and 3,535.2 seconds"; ERS-011 has cheap breadth arms adjudicated against the same union as the strong arm.
suggested_repair: Add the frozen research artifacts of the topic's other arms as an admitted input class for the review and breadth stages, and narrow the negative constraint to the five research stages.

claim: ERS-009 and SSYS-037 both assign the defaults of the four limits to External Research, but no unit in the compile states a default for any of them, and only the turn budget is deferred by an open question.
evidence: ERS-009: "this owner fixes their meaning, their defaults and the rule that a job reports which limit ended it"; SSYS-037: "Their meaning, their defaults and the rule that every job reports which limit ended it belong to Plans/External_Research.md (ERS-008, ERS-009)". No default value appears in ERS-008, ERS-009, ERS-012 or SSYS-037; the evidence shard's cost-policy.json row establishes "per-job 40 responses and 2,400 seconds, lifetime caps", and ERS-012 uses 2,400 s only as a measured fact about continuation 4. q-001 defers only the turn budget.
suggested_repair: State the default for the cost cap, the per-job wall-seconds limit, the lifetime cap and the unresolved-usage disposition in ERS-009 with the run that established each, or record an open question for each one still undecided.

claim: The record field the evidence names for the limit that ended a job, bound_by, is declared preserved in ERS-009 but appears nowhere, so the obligation and the contract fixture that turns on it have no named field.
evidence: ERS-009 declares preserved_exact_tokens: ["bound_by", "per-job limit", ...]; the text only says "A job's terminal record names the limit that bound it". The evidence shard's continuation4/README row establishes "job status and bound_by". ATS-054's negatives include "that an adapter label is not an admissible source for the limit that bound a job" without naming a field either.
suggested_repair: Name the terminal record's bound_by field in ERS-009 and in the contract family so the negative fixture has a field to mutate.

claim: ERS-010 states as canon a general claim the campaign did not establish and that ERS-011 explicitly contradicts one unit later, and it is the stated justification for ERS-010's product rule.
evidence: ERS-010: "A topic's review stage runs one strong model with a turn budget sized to finish every job, because on identical inputs review models differ in depth rather than in kind". ERS-011: "one of the three, at 0.82 dollars, held three findings no other review arm reached, so the review arms differ in depth and, at the margin, in kind". The evidence shard's proper-subset result is one arm against its own control at two ceilings, not a result across review models; the atom's negative constraints say "Do not promise a stage, bound or figure the September 2026 campaign did not exercise" and "Do not ... generalize one frozen case into a ranking", and ERS-010's own negative constraint repeats it.
suggested_repair: Restate ERS-010's justification as the measured proper-subset result for one arm against its own control, and let ERS-011 carry the at-the-margin difference in kind.

claim: Three units cite an out-of-repository experiment path with the leading /mnt/Cursor/ removed, so the source_lineage entry reads as a repository-relative path that does not resolve.
evidence: ERS-010 and ERS-013 cite "PM-Experiments/research-audit-native-20260907/process-pilot-20260908/REVIEW_ADJUDICATION_20260916.md" and ERS-012 cites "PM-Experiments/research-audit-native-20260907/process-pilot-20260908/BRIEF_GOAL3_RESEARCH_CANON_20260917.md", while the evidence and authorization shards give both as absolute paths beginning "/mnt/Cursor/PM-Experiments/...". Every other source_lineage entry in the compile is genuinely repository-relative (reports/..., Plans/...).
suggested_repair: Write the two experiment sources as their absolute /mnt/Cursor paths with the SHA-256 the evidence shard records, so they cannot be read as repository paths.

claim: Two provenance terms ERS-014 declares preserved, one of them an owner-atom exact token, appear nowhere in the unit.
evidence: ERS-014 declares preserved_exact_tokens: ["protocol fingerprint", "runtime identity", "output manifest", "quiesce"]; the text says "pins the protocol freeze hash" and "two runs sharing a fingerprint" but never "protocol fingerprint", and "Every frozen output tree carries a SHA-256 manifest" but never "output manifest". atom-external-research-owner-canon lists "protocol fingerprint" among its exact tokens, and the cited sources are protocol-fingerprints.json and output-manifests.json.
suggested_repair: Use the terms protocol fingerprint and output manifest in ERS-014's canonical text where the records are named.

claim: PLS-023 declares it preserves "standing repair authorization", an exact token of its own atom, but never names the authorization a correction lands under, so the landing-boundary unit describes the gates without the authority behind them.
evidence: atom-research-landing-ledger-consumer exact_tokens: ["standing repair authorization", "currentness", "independent review", "ledger question record"]. PLS-023 declares the first of those preserved but its text says only "a correction still requires its currentness re-check and independent review and a capability or product choice still requires the user's recorded answer". The phrase occurs in no PLS-023 sentence; ERS-006 is the only unit that uses it.
suggested_repair: Name the standing repair authorization in PLS-023's canonical text where the correction path is described.

claim: The compile places obligations on three owners that get neither a consumer reference nor a recorded follow-up, although q-004 records exactly that gap for the three owners the concurrent branch was holding.
evidence: ERS-001 splits ownership with "usage semantics by usage-feature" and ERS-008 lists Plans/usage-feature.md in implementation_surfaces and owner_hints; ERS-007 lists Plans/Planning_Wizard.md in implementation_surfaces and says "execution follows the existing Approve And Build path"; ERS-010 and ERS-011 carry "ContractRef: ... ContractName:Plans/Models_System.md". The authorization admits consumer references only in assistant-chat-design, Planning_Ledger_System and Settings_System, and open_items records a follow-up only for Jujutsu_Integration, Source_Control_System and Backup_Restore_System.

claim: Three of the four consumer units are appended without the heading and ContractRef line that every other unit in the compile carries, so they differ in house shape from SSYS-037, which was appended the same way.
evidence: ERS-001 to ERS-014 each begin "### ERS-0NN - <Title>" and end with a "ContractRef: ..." line, and SSYS-037 begins "### SSYS-037 - External Research Limit Values" with a "ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Settings_System.md, ContractName:Plans/External_Research.md" line. ACD-467, PLS-023 and ATS-054 begin directly with the yaml fence and carry no ContractRef line at all.

claim: compiled_plan_outputs omits the derived files this branch regenerates, while listing one derived file, so the landing reviewer cannot use it as the list of what the compile changed.
evidence: compiled_plan_outputs lists "Plans/00-plans-index.md" together with the owner documents, contract files, sharding_config and the verifier script, but no Plans/_shards/** file and no Plans/.plan_index file. q-004's detail states the two branches share "the six Plans/.plan_index files that both regenerate".

claim: Four units declare preserved_exact_tokens that appear nowhere in the unit, and in ERS-005 the declaration contradicts the unit's own rule against restating the response set.
evidence: ERS-005 declares ["Approve", "Deny", "Deny with changes", "Ask a question"] while its canonical_text says the response set is "owned by Decision_Log DL-036 and assistant-chat-design and are referenced here, never restated" and its negative constraint forbids restating it; "Deny with changes" and "Ask a question" occur nowhere in it. ERS-007 declares "accepted for planning" and "unapproved optional capability", neither of which occurs (the text says "a deferred or unapproved item"). ERS-008 declares "native records" (text has "native usage records"). ERS-013 declares "same family" (text has "shares a model family" and "shared-family"). ACD-467 legitimately carries the four responses.
suggested_repair: Make each unit's preserved_exact_tokens list the strings the unit actually carries, and drop the response set from ERS-005.

claim: The depends_on and unblocks edges disagree in both directions across the compile, so the reverse-edge view of the new owner's graph is not the forward view.
evidence: ERS-001 unblocks ERS-002 to ERS-014 but only ERS-002 lists ERS-001 in depends_on; ERS-008 depends_on ERS-002 while ERS-002 unblocks only [ERS-003, ERS-004, ERS-012]; ERS-003 unblocks ERS-013 while ERS-013 depends_on [ERS-004, ERS-010]; ACD-467, PLS-023 and SSYS-037 depend on ERS-005, ERS-006 and ERS-009 respectively, none of which lists them in unblocks; ATS-054 depends_on only [ATS-046] although its whole subject is the External Research contract family and its source_lineage cites ERS-001.
suggested_repair: Regenerate the edges so each depends_on has its matching unblocks, and add the ERS-001 edge to ATS-054.

claim: Two units take their lineage from a source the evidence shard says is still being appended to, so the hash recorded for it cannot be reproduced on a later re-check.
evidence: The evidence shard row reads "REVIEW_ADJUDICATION_20260916.md (appended to after this reading; the hash is the 2026-09-17 snapshot, not a frozen file)" with SHA-256 8a7358bc...; ERS-010 and ERS-013 both cite that file in source_lineage, and ERS-006 requires a correction's evidence to be named "by path and SHA-256" for the currentness re-check.
suggested_repair: Freeze a copy of the reviewed revision under the campaign report tree and cite that frozen path instead.

The authorization shard admits "this ledger, registered and validated, with every source cited by path and SHA-256"; the evidence table has no row for that verification.json.

claim: One of the five defects the cited corrections record establishes, the shared temp-file name, is carried by no unit, while the other four each landed as an obligation.
evidence: The evidence shard's continuation4/corrections.json row establishes "The stream-block response count, the post-response boundary defect, the shared temp-file name, the hardcoded runtime version, and the 41-against-40 reading". Stream blocks and the post-response boundary are in ERS-008's negative constraints, the hardcoded runtime version is in ERS-014's, and the 41-against-40 reading is in ERS-009's acceptance. No unit mentions temp-file naming, per-job isolation or concurrent-arm interference.
